key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves multiscale CFD next-step velocity reconstruction by combining hybrid spectral encoding, PDE-residual-guided attention, and self-supervised pretraining.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical surrogate model for accelerating real-world flow simulation while preserving localized wake and fluid-structure interaction features that are often missed by global-only models.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding captures both global flow trends and localized multiscale structures.
Physics-biased self-attention uses PDE residual diagnostics to steer the model toward physically consistent regions.
Self-supervised pretraining with Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction improves representation learning.
evidence_signal: Across cylinder-wake and fluid-structure interaction benchmarks, the model achieved the best reported aggregate accuracy, including 0.05875 all-channel NMSE and 0.97019 PCC on cylinder wake, and 2.70 × 10^-4 all-channel NMSE on FSI versus 4.02 × 10^-4 for the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on two benchmark cases, so broader robustness across more complex geometries, boundary conditions, and longer rollout horizons still needs validation.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
